neighboring_unit_entries.title: Large values replace pointwise RH bounds in moment control
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source explains why known unconditional upper bounds are sparse, distinguishes RH from Lindelof, and contrasts a weak pointwise RH consequence with Soundararajan's essentially sharp full-interval moment bound based on the distribution of log|zeta|.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Log|zeta| tails have Gaussian and V log V regimes
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 4 partitions the admissible large-value range into two near-Gaussian decay regimes and a far-tail V log V regime, with explicit theta-dependent losses suited to a short interval.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: On fixed-power short intervals, the unconditional lower bound and RH-conditional upper bound identify H times a k-squared logarithmic power as the common scale up to the stated vanishing loss.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The upper bound assumes RH and H=T^theta with fixed theta, while the lower bound covers integer k and much shorter intervals.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Discretized tails reduce the moment bound to a quadratic maximum
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Small and very large values are disposed of directly, the middle range is discretized, and multiplying its measure by exp(2kU) reduces the problem to maximizing a concave quadratic, recovering the k-squared logarithmic exponent.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: RH supplies a prime-polynomial majorant; high-moment estimates yield piecewise tail decay; discretizing and optimizing those tails yields the moment exponent.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The chain is solver- and parameter-specific analytic evidence, depends on fixed theta, and retains an O(1/log_3 T) exponent loss.
